subject: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch

Hi Elena —

Congrats again on getting the internal OK for the pilot next week. We ran the numbers after your traffic profile and have one recommendation to avoid dropped requests during your busiest 2-hour window: a temporary throughput uplift (higher request rate quota) for the launch window on Nov 20–22.

What we'd propose:
- 3x the standard burst quota for the 2-hour daily peak (UTC 15:00–17:00) for three consecutive days (Nov 20–22).
- Maintain latency SLO (95th pct < 220ms) for provisioned capacity.
- A mutual rollback clause: if average utilization outside the peak exceeds 75% for more than 6 hours, we revert to baseline.

Operational notes: we will enable the uplift from our side and place a monitoring hook into your Dashboard so both teams can observe queue depth and token spend in real time. There is a small surcharge for reserved burst capacity; I'll compile a short amendment to the MSA for signature if you want to proceed.

Attaching a one-page uplift request with estimated cost impact. Can you confirm procurement contact and whether Sentry needs SLA credit language in the amendment?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if easier.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
Attachment: sentry_uplift_request_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sentryhealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement looped in here. A few clarifying Qs before we escalate to legal:
- Can you confirm the uplift is limited to request-rate (RPS) and does not change token-based billing?
- We need explicit language about SLA credits if latency targets are missed during the uplift window. Our legal will require a commensurate credit (pro-rated) if 95th percentile exceeds 250ms for more than one peak hour across the three days.
- Who will own post-peak cleanup if a backlog forms (retries, webhooks)?

If you can provide a redlineable amendment (DocuSign-ready) with those items, procurement will move quickly.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product Partnerships, SentryHealth
elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch

Hi Elena — looping in legal ops / contracts POV and engineering runbook. 

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Billing: uplift affects request-rate quota only; token billing stays as-is. We will include an explicit statement in the amendment to that effect.
- SLA credits: we can accept a pro-rated credit trigger at 95th > 250ms for >1 peak hour as you requested. Our standard credit is 5% of the monthly API fees for an SLO miss; for the temporary uplift window we suggest converting that to a per-day pro-rated value (we've drafted language in the attached MPA redline).
- Backlog ownership: Redwood will throttle and drop non-idempotent requests once the backlog threshold is reached; for webhooks/retries we recommend SentryHealth implement an exponential backoff. We'll include an operational playbook in the amendment to document expected retry behavior and alerting.

I've attached a redline (MPA) that includes:
- Amendment section with the uplift schedule and surcharge table
- SLA credit wording tied to the uplift window
- Monitoring and runbook summary

If those points look good, we can produce a DocuSign envelope today.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sentry_mpa_redlines.docx (DOCX, 32KB)

From: procurement@sentryhealth.com <procurement@sentryhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch

Marissa, Jonas —

Procurement reviewed the redline. Two items before we can sign:
1) We require the surcharge table to include a hard cap on daily spend for the uplift days (Sentry will not accept uncapped surcharges). Please add a max daily surcharge equal to 150% of the average daily API spend for the month preceding the uplift.
2) Add a 14-day post-launch reconciliation period where both sides reconcile actual request volumes vs. estimated; any overage beyond the cap will be credited back if caused by Redwood routing anomalies.

If you can incorporate those two items, procurement is comfortable executing the amendment via DocuSign.

Thanks,
SentryHealth Procurement
procurement@sentryhealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: procurement@sentryhealth.com, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: SLA amendment request: temporary throughput uplift for Nov launch

Thanks — understood and agreed in principle. We'll update the amendment with:
- Max daily surcharge cap = 150% of prior-month average daily API spend (we'll compute and insert the dollar amount).
- 14-day reconciliation window with explicit credit back for overages attributable to Redwood routing errors.

I'll have Legal Ops push the updated DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow. Once executed, our ops team will schedule the uplift and provision monitoring access for Sentry's engineering leads.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com
DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-sentry-amendment
